flashcards.q: What are the four defects of VLOOKUP that XLOOKUP fixes in one signature?
flashcards.a: 1) Direction-independence (return array separate from lookup array -- insert-column breakage ends), 2) exact match is the DEFAULT (VLOOKUP's approximate default silently returns wrong values), 3) if_not_found built in (no IFERROR wrap), 4) search_mode -1 searches last-to-first for most-recent match. Plus multi-column return spills.

flashcards.q: What is a spill range, the # operator, and #SPILL!?
flashcards.a: One formula owns a live output range that auto-resizes on recalc; E2# references the whole spill; #SPILL! = the range is blocked by existing content (spills never overwrite -- a safety property). Diagnosis of a new #SPILL!: someone inserted content inside the claimed range.

flashcards.q: Why does LET make formulas faster, not just more readable?
flashcards.a: Excel computes each named value ONCE and caches it -- a SUM over 500k rows referenced three times in a formula costs one pass, not three. Binding = local variable with evaluate-once semantics.

flashcards.q: How does SCAN replace the dragged running-total formula, and what does it generalize to?
flashcards.a: =SCAN(0, C2:C6, LAMBDA(acc, v, acc + v)) spills the whole running-total column from ONE formula. Any accumulating logic (running max, concatenation) by changing the LAMBDA body.

flashcards.q: What is the live top-3 composition, and which legacy pattern does each function replace?
flashcards.a: =TAKE(SORTBY(names, sales, -1), 3). TAKE/SORTBY <- manual sorting+slicing; UNIQUE <- Remove Duplicates; FILTER <- AutoFilter+helper columns; TEXTSPLIT <- Text-to-Columns; IFS <- nested IF pyramids; SEQUENCE <- fill-handle dragging.

flashcards.q: Why is LAMBDA significant beyond custom functions?
flashcards.a: Saved in Name Manager it becomes a callable function with named parameters, no VBA/macros/security warnings -- and LAMBDAs recurse (can call themselves by saved name), making Excel Turing-complete without macros.

flashcards.q: What is @ (implicit intersection) and what does encountering it tell you?
flashcards.a: The legacy compatibility shim that silences a spill to one value. Seeing @ means a modern formula was opened in a legacy file context or pasted into a pre-dynamic-array workbook -- the @ is the tell that the workbook predates 2019.

flashcards.q: Name the volatile functions and the failure mode they cause.
flashcards.a: INDIRECT, OFFSET, TODAY, NOW, RAND (RANDARRAY is volatile-on-edit). They force recalculation of everything downstream on every change -- recalc storms in large sheets. Replace with structured references and LET-cached values.

flashcards.q: Why is VLOOKUP's approximate-match default described as silently dangerous?
flashcards.a: Approximate match assumes ascending-sorted data: on unsorted data it returns a WRONG VALUE, not an error -- the failure is invisible. This is the single most damaging Excel bug in the wild, and why exact-match-default in XLOOKUP matters.

flashcards.q: What are the three tiers of the modern Excel stack and what does each own?
flashcards.a: Power Query owns ETL (clean/shape/merge -- inspectable refreshable steps); the Data Model owns relationships and measures (DAX); the formula tier owns live analysis. Production failures are boundary violations: ETL in formulas, modeling in mega-formulas.

flashcards.q: Why do Tables (Ctrl+T) matter specifically with dynamic arrays?
flashcards.a: Structured references (Sales[Amount]) auto-expand as data grows -- formulas and spills track the table's size without $-range surgery. The two features are designed together; non-Table ranges strand dragged formulas when rows are added.

flashcards.q: What's the query-folding concept and why check it early?
flashcards.a: Power Query steps that FOLD run as SQL on the source database; steps that break folding (complex merges, index columns) run in memory. A 'refresh' that downloads the warehouse instead of folding is an outage in waiting -- check folding before building more steps.

flashcards.q: When would you still use INDEX/MATCH in 2026?
flashcards.a: Pre-2021 Excel builds and legacy-team conventions (the lingua franca of 2016 shops and pre-2020 tutorial cohorts). Volunteer XLOOKUP, write INDEX/MATCH fluently, know the exact-match-default difference by heart.

flashcards.q: What is the honest Excel-vs-pandas boundary?
flashcards.a: Excel's edge is the last mile: stakeholders can touch intermediate values. Above ~1M rows (hard cap 1,048,576) or ~50 workbooks of duplicated logic, it's warehouse/notebook work. The skill is recognizing the boundary, not defending either side.

flashcards.q: What's the difference between IFS and nested IF, and what is the catch-all pattern?
flashcards.a: IFS reads condition-result pairs top-to-bottom with no parenthesis counting; nested IF gets unreadable past 2-3 levels. The final TRUE acts as the else catch-all: IFS(C2>120000, 'Senior', C2>80000, 'Mid', TRUE, 'Junior').
